events.title: Pope Paschal I crowns Lothar co-emperor in Rome
events.description: On Easter Sunday Pope Paschal I crowned Lothar, son of Louis the Pious, as co-emperor in St Peter's. The ceremony reinforced the idea that imperial legitimacy came through papal coronation in Rome.
events.html: On Easter Sunday Pope Paschal I crowned Lothar, son of Louis the Pious, as co-emperor in St Peter's. The ceremony reinforced the idea that imperial legitimacy came through papal coronation in Rome.

events.title: The Fatimids launch their second invasion of Abbasid Egypt
events.description: The Fatimid Caliphate began its second invasion of Egypt, then under Abbasid rule, led again by the heir-apparent al-Qa'im bi-Amr Allah. The Fatimids took Alexandria with ease, but the campaign, which lasted until 921, ended in failure.

events.title: Alexander Nevsky defeats the Teutonic Order on frozen Lake Peipus
events.description: Novgorod's forces under Prince Alexander Nevsky beat the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order in the Battle on the Ice, halting the Order's eastward expansion into Russian lands.
events.html: Novgorod's forces under Prince Alexander Nevsky beat the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order in the Battle on the Ice, halting the Order's eastward expansion into Russian lands.

events.title: Jacob Roggeveen reaches Easter Island
events.description: Dutch navigator Jacob Roggeveen became the first known European to reach Rapa Nui, naming it after the day of his arrival, Easter Sunday. His crew recorded the island's great stone moai.
events.html: Dutch navigator Jacob Roggeveen became the first known European to reach Rapa Nui, naming it after the day of his arrival, Easter Sunday. His crew recorded the island's great stone moai.

events.title: George Washington issues the first presidential veto
events.description: Washington vetoed a bill apportioning seats in the House of Representatives, judging it unconstitutional. It was the first use of a power that later presidents would wield thousands of times.
events.html: Washington vetoed a bill apportioning seats in the House of Representatives, judging it unconstitutional. It was the first use of a power that later presidents would wield thousands of times.

events.title: Chile declares war on Peru and Bolivia
events.description: Chile's declaration opened the War of the Pacific, fought over the nitrate-rich Atacama Desert. Victory gave Chile the coastal provinces and left Bolivia without access to the sea.
events.html: Chile's declaration opened the War of the Pacific, fought over the nitrate-rich Atacama Desert. Victory gave Chile the coastal provinces and left Bolivia without access to the sea.

events.title: Winston Churchill resigns as Prime Minister
events.description: Aged 80 and in failing health, Winston Churchill stepped down as Prime Minister and was succeeded by Anthony Eden. It closed a career at the top of British politics spanning more than half a century.
events.html: Aged 80 and in failing health, Winston Churchill stepped down as Prime Minister and was succeeded by Anthony Eden. It closed a career at the top of British politics spanning more than half a century.

events.title: Nirvana's Kurt Cobain dies in Seattle
events.description: Kurt Cobain, singer and guitarist of Nirvana, died at his Seattle home aged 27; his body was found three days later. His death closed the band that had carried grunge into the mainstream.
